literature_notes: Both ledger lines (L1, L2) describe the same experimental system: PCDH7 isoforms subcloned into the retroviral vector pQCXIP-EGFP-N1 at EcoRI/AgeI sites, producing a C-terminal EGFP fusion. In the standard pEGFP-N1 architecture the MCS is upstream of EGFP, so the insert is fused N-terminally to EGFP and the fluorescent tag lands at the protein C-terminus (after residue 1069). PCDH7 is a single-pass type-I transmembrane protein whose C-terminus (residues 901–1069) is intracellular per the authoritative topology landmarks. The co-localization with E-cadherin at cell–cell contacts (L1) confirms correct membrane trafficking of the full-length construct, but the EGFP tag itself faces the cytoplasm. This is an intracellular tag and does not qualify as an extracellular surface-tag site under the ledger rules. No ledger line describes a tag inserted at the extracellular N-terminus (after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 28) or anywhere within the extracellular domain (residues 29–879). Zero extracellular sites are supported.

literature_other_positions.note: PCDH7 subcloned into pQCXIP-EGFP-N1 (EcoRI/AgeI) places EGFP at the protein C-terminus (after residue 1069), which lies in the intracellular domain (residues 901–1069); the tagged construct traffics to the membrane (L1) but the tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
